affect.q: Are the emotions discrete categories, or positions on two dimensions?
affect.verdict: PASS — Ekman 1993 affirms discrete states and names the valence/arousal rival he rejects; Posner/Russell/Peterson 2005 affirm the two-system dimensional model and state it stands in contrast to basic-emotions discreteness. Direct affirm/deny on the same proposition.

affect.q: Is an emotion a bodily change, or a judgment?
affect.verdict: PASS — James 1884 identifies the emotion with the feeling of bodily change; the cognitivist account (Scarantino and de Sousa, SEP) identifies it with a judgment. The identifications exclude each other; the dossier honestly leaves which is right open.

affect.q: Does the gambling task show guidance before reportable knowledge?
affect.verdict: PASS — Bechara et al. 1997: performance preceded by a nonconscious biasing step; Maia and McClelland 2004: reportable knowledge accounts for the choices, 'no need to appeal to nonconscious somatic markers'. Head-on on the same task's interpretation; the dossier bounds what the comparison settles.

attention.q: Where does selection happen: early or late?
attention.verdict: PASS with qualification — the early/late traditions give opposite answers on whether distractors are excluded from perceptual processing; Lavie 2005's load resolution honestly reframed (perceptual load and cognitive-control load move distractor processing in opposite directions) rather than settled. Live dispute recorded as such.

attention.q: Does a wandering mind cost more than it returns?
attention.verdict: UNRESOLVED on the strict same-conditions test — Killingsworth and Gilbert 2010 measure average mood while wandering; Mooneyham and Schooler 2013 accept the costs and propose boundary functions. The dossier itself records that the two papers do not contradict each other's measurements; live dispute with the qualification preserved.

PASS — Jonides's two-process model (focused/diffuse modes) vs Eriksen and Yeh's zoom lens, proposed explicitly as an alternative to two processing modes; Johnson and Yantis 1995 rejected the two-state mixture prediction. The dossier honestly notes the parallel-sampling result does not by itself establish the zoom lens.

motivation.verdict: PASS — Deci/Koestner/Ryan 1999 meta-analysis (contingent rewards undermine, d = -0.28 to -0.40) vs Cameron/Banko/Pierce meta-analysis ('rewards are not harmful to motivation'). Competing meta-analyses, opposite bottom lines on the same proposition.

motivation.q: Do needs line up in a hierarchy of prepotency?
motivation.verdict: PASS — Maslow 1943 affirms the prepotency ordering; Wahba and Bridwell 1976 review of the tests finds little clear or consistent support. The dossier bounds the review to the testable propositions.

motivation.q: Can reason alone move a person to act?
motivation.verdict: PASS with qualification — Hume: reason alone can never be a motive; Kant: the will determined by the maxim, respect self-wrought by a rational concept. The dossier narrows the dispute honestly (Kant grants a feeling, arising from the thought) and records its own lean and limits.

overload-overwhelm.q: Is the capacity to keep going a limited resource?
overload-overwhelm.verdict: PASS with qualification — Baumeister et al. 1998 affirms the limited shared resource; Hagger et al. 2016 RRR is null-compatible (d = 0.04, CI [-0.07, 0.15]) — absence of detection, not an explicit denial; the dossier adds the 12-lab partial replication and honestly treats the model as unsettled.

overload-overwhelm.q: Does a larger set of options overload the chooser?
overload-overwhelm.verdict: PASS — Scheibehenne/Greifeneder/Todd 2010 (mean effect virtually zero) vs Chernev/Böckenholt/Goodman 2015 (significant once moderators accounted; explicitly 'counter to the data reported by prior meta-analytic research'). Head-on between meta-analyses; abstracts-only limit recorded honestly.

overload-overwhelm.q: Is rest for the sake of work, or work for the sake of rest?
overload-overwhelm.verdict: PASS — intra-Aristotelian: NE X.6 'Relaxation, then, is not an end; for it is taken for the sake of activity' vs NE X.7 'we are busy that we may have leisure'. Both sides the same author's own text, opposite orderings on the same proposition.
